questions.prompt: Which qualification is retained in the statement about humanity and difficult conditions?
questions.promptZh: 关于人性与艰难处境的句子，哪种限定应当保留？
options: Every disaster inevitably brings out the best in every person.
The author says the best of humanity often emerges from the worst conditions.
The author states that suffering has no possible relation to human strength.
The sentence provides experimental proof that the worse the event, the happier everyone becomes.
optionsZh: 每场灾难必然让每个人显出最好的一面。
作者说最艰难的处境中常显出人性最好的一面。
作者说苦难与人的力量绝无可能联系。
句子提供实验性证明：事件越糟，每人就越幸福。
analyses: A often 不等于每次必然，句中也没有 every person。
B 保留 often 及 best/worst 对照，是此处的概括性哲学讨论。
C 与 comes out of 的联系相反。
D 本句不是实验结果，best of humanity 也不等于人人主观幸福。

vocabulary.meaning: 源自；从某种处境中显现
vocabulary.context: 这里是品质在处境中显现，不是人物从某房间走出。
vocabulary.example: A new determination sometimes comes out of a difficult period.
collocations: comes out of the worst conditions

questions.evidenceQuote: The philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche thought of earthquakes as a sort of catharsis, saying, “Earthquakes bury many wells and leave many languishing, but they also bring to light inner powers and secrets.” As an expert on classical philosophy, Nietzsche was cognizant of the ancient world. In ancient Greeks he saw the greatest human strength at a time of crisis: the will to live and to re-create. The best of humanity often comes out of the worst conditions.

questions.prompt: How does the author characterise Nietzsche's essay titles?
questions.promptZh: 作者如何形容 Nietzsche 的文章标题？
options: As technical labels for three measured laboratory outcomes.
As titles chosen by other people against Nietzsche's wishes.
As modest titles that avoid any mention of his own abilities.
As comically self-praising titles about his wisdom, cleverness, and good books.
optionsZh: 三种实测实验结果的技术标签。
其他人违背 Nietzsche 意愿选的标题。
避免提及自己能力的谦逊标题。
关于自己智慧、聪明和好书的幽默自赞标题。
analyses: A 标题不是实验变量或结果标签。
B Nietzsche wrote essays...entitled 未说他人强加。
C 三个 Why I... 标题恰强调自身长处，非完全回避。
D comically 限定诙谐语气，三个标题的对象均保留；作者未据此验证这些自赞都客观成立。

vocabulary.meaning: 滑稽地；带幽默意味地
vocabulary.context: 修饰标题的呈现方式，不能略去而只理解为严肃自我认证。
vocabulary.example: The essay was comically entitled as if the writer could explain every success.

questions.evidenceQuote: Nietzsche wrote essays comically entitled “Why I Am So Wise,” “Why I Am So Clever,” and “Why I Write Such Good Books.” He was a funny guy. How did he have so many insights? Nietzsche credited his illness.

questions.prompt: What does 'a funny guy' mean in the immediate context?
questions.promptZh: 紧接这些标题，a funny guy 在这里是什么意思？
options: A person with a sense of humour, as the author presents him.
A solemn writer whose essay titles are presented without any humour.
A writer criticised here for having no insights.
An author amusing only because other people imposed the titles on him.
optionsZh: 作者笔下一个有幽默感的人。
其文章标题被毫无幽默意味地呈现的严肃作者。
在这里被批评完全没有洞见的作者。
仅因别人强加标题才好笑的作者。
analyses: A 前句 comically 与自赞标题支持幽默有趣的语气。
B comically 明示幽默，不能反读成毫无幽默。
C 后句反问为何有这么多洞见，非批评没有洞见。
D 没有别人强加标题的叙述；funny 描述的是作者此处的人物语气。

vocabulary.meaning: 有趣、有幽默感的人
vocabulary.context: 承接文章标题的诙谐，不是对病情的专业术语。
vocabulary.example: After reading the playful titles, she called the writer a funny guy.

questions.evidenceQuote: Nietzsche wrote essays comically entitled “Why I Am So Wise,” “Why I Am So Clever,” and “Why I Write Such Good Books.” He was a funny guy. How did he have so many insights? Nietzsche credited his illness.

questions.prompt: What does the question about Nietzsche's many insights prepare the reader for?
questions.promptZh: 关于 Nietzsche 何来许多洞见的问句，为下文什么内容作铺垫？
options: A calculation of the number of words in each essay title.
A guarantee that insight is inherited and cannot be influenced by experience.
His own attribution of those insights to illness.
An announcement that he had never experienced illness.
optionsZh: 计算每个文章标题的词数。
保证洞见遗传而绝不受经历影响。
他把这些洞见归功于疾病的解释。
宣布他从未患病。
analyses: A so many insights 问来源，不是标题长度。
B 原文并未提出遗传决定说。
C 下一句 Nietzsche credited his illness 回应 How，明确归属为他自己的解释。
D 后句直接提 illness，不能读成从无患病。

vocabulary.meaning: 洞见；深入理解事物的认识
vocabulary.context: 在此指其思想认识，不是肉眼视力或文章的页数。
vocabulary.example: The philosopher reflected on the source of his insights.

questions.evidenceQuote: Nietzsche wrote essays comically entitled “Why I Am So Wise,” “Why I Am So Clever,” and “Why I Write Such Good Books.” He was a funny guy. How did he have so many insights? Nietzsche credited his illness.

questions.prompt: Which appointment is described in the biographical sentence?
questions.promptZh: 传记句描述了哪次任命？
options: In 1876, at twenty-four, he became chair of economics at Basel.
In 1869, at twenty-four, he became chair of classical philology at Basel, the youngest appointed to that post.
In 1869, he retired from Basel after serving there for twenty-four years.
In 1876, he was appointed to study only modern laboratory medicine.
optionsZh: 1876 年，二十四岁，任 Basel 经济学教席。
1869 年，二十四岁，任 Basel 古典语文学教席，是该职位最年轻任职者。
1869 年，在 Basel 任职二十四年后退休。
1876 年，获任只研究现代实验医学。
analyses: A 将后文请假年份1876挪到任命，且改学科。
B 年份、年龄、学校、学科及最年轻任该职位五项对应。
C twenty-four 指年龄而非任期，appointed 也不是退休。
D 古典语文学不是实验医学；括号明确说明它研究语言历史。

vocabulary.meaning: 语文学；语言及其历史的研究
vocabulary.context: 原书括号为 study of the history of languages，不能误认成 physiology 生理学。
vocabulary.example: Her work in philology examined the history of languages.

questions.evidenceQuote: In 1869, at age twenty-four, he was appointed chair of classical philology (the study of the history of languages) at Basel University, the youngest ever appointed to the post. In 1876, an illness forced him to take leave from Basel. This prolonged illness gave him a chance to change his habits completely. It helped him detach himself from typical conventions.

questions.prompt: Why did Nietzsche take leave from Basel in 1876?
questions.promptZh: Nietzsche 在 1876 年为何从 Basel 请假？
options: He retired immediately on being appointed in 1869.
He voluntarily took a break solely to accept a new university post.
He left because he had completed all his research and had nothing left to think about.
An illness forced him to take leave.
optionsZh: 他在1869年刚获任时立即退休。
他纯为接受另一大学职位而自愿休假。
他因研究全部完成、再无可思考的问题而离开。
疾病迫使他请假。
analyses: A 1869是任命，1876才是此句请假；appointed不是retired。
B forced与自愿不同，且没有接受新职位的原因。
C 后面还要谈思想与习惯变化，原句未给研究完毕的原因。
D an illness forced him 明确给请假原因；take leave 不自动等于被开除或永久辞职。

vocabulary.meaning: 请假；暂时离开岗位
vocabulary.context: 此处由疾病迫使其离岗，不是凭该短语就可确认永久解职。
vocabulary.example: The lecturer had to take leave because of illness.

questions.evidenceQuote: In 1869, at age twenty-four, he was appointed chair of classical philology (the study of the history of languages) at Basel University, the youngest ever appointed to the post. In 1876, an illness forced him to take leave from Basel. This prolonged illness gave him a chance to change his habits completely. It helped him detach himself from typical conventions.

questions.prompt: What necessity did Nietzsche say illness bestowed on him?
questions.promptZh: Nietzsche 说疾病赋予他什么必要状态？
options: Lying still, having leisure, waiting, and being patient.
Travelling continuously with no rest or waiting.
Reading every available book without time for reflection.
Immediately returning to the same professional routine without any change.
optionsZh: 静卧、闲暇、等待和耐心。
连续旅行，绝不停歇等待。
读遍所有书，没有反思时间。
立即回到毫无变化的原有职业惯例。
analyses: A 四个 of 并列的内容逐项保留，来自他后来的回忆。
B 与 lying still、waiting 方向相反。
C 后文甚至说 stopped reading and started thinking。
D 此处强调习惯被打断后的状态，不是马上照旧；回忆不构成对所有病人的统一效果。

vocabulary.meaning: 赋予我；给予我某种东西
vocabulary.context: 本句把疾病带来的被迫状态写成赋予，带回顾性的修辞意味。
vocabulary.example: The unexpected pause bestowed on me a chance to reflect.

questions.evidenceQuote: He later recalled that “it permitted, it commanded me to forget; it bestowed on me the necessity of lying still, of leisure, of waiting and being patient. But that means, of thinking.” In his sickness, he stopped reading and started thinking. Looking back on his life, Nietzsche said that he was never happier with himself than in the sickest and most painful periods of his life.

questions.prompt: What does Nietzsche say the enforced stillness and leisure meant?
questions.promptZh: Nietzsche 说被迫静卧和闲暇意味着什么？
options: That thought had become physically impossible for him.
That no time had been available for any mental activity.
An opportunity or necessity for thinking.
A requirement to resume reading immediately and stop reflecting.
optionsZh: 他已在生理上不可能思考。
没有任何进行精神活动的时间。
有机会或必要进行思考。
必须立即恢复阅读、停止反思。
analyses: A of thinking 是肯定指向思考，不是不能思考。
B 承接 leisure/waiting，正有反思空间。
C But that means, of thinking 把前面的状态重新理解为思考；需连前句回忆读，不能当独立完整论证。
D 后句 stopped reading and started thinking 与选项反向。

vocabulary.meaning: 思考；反思
vocabulary.context: 在回忆中与静卧、等待的状态相连，区别机械保持原有阅读习惯。
vocabulary.example: The quiet interval became a period of thinking.

questions.evidenceQuote: He later recalled that “it permitted, it commanded me to forget; it bestowed on me the necessity of lying still, of leisure, of waiting and being patient. But that means, of thinking.” In his sickness, he stopped reading and started thinking. Looking back on his life, Nietzsche said that he was never happier with himself than in the sickest and most painful periods of his life.

questions.prompt: Which account matches Nietzsche's retrospective statement about himself?
questions.promptZh: 哪种叙述符合 Nietzsche 回望自己时的说法？
options: He reported that every person is happiest whenever they are ill.
He said he had never been happier with himself than during his sickest and most painful periods.
He said he was satisfied with himself only during pain-free periods.
He denied ever having any painful period in his life.
optionsZh: 他报告每个人只要患病就最快乐。
他说自己从未比在最病痛时期更满意自己。
他说自己只有在完全无痛的时期才对自己满意。
他否认人生中曾有任何痛苦时期。
analyses: A 原文是 he said 和 with himself，不是每个人的普遍幸福结论。
B 保留回顾性自述、比较与对自己满意的对象。
C 将最病痛时期的自我满意反转为仅在无痛时满意，比较方向错误。
D sickest and most painful periods 明示病痛，非否认存在。

vocabulary.meaning: 对他自己；在自我评价方面
vocabulary.context: happier with himself 强调对自己的满意，不能直接改作身体更健康或疼痛全消。
vocabulary.example: He felt more satisfied with himself despite the difficult circumstances.

questions.evidenceQuote: He later recalled that “it permitted, it commanded me to forget; it bestowed on me the necessity of lying still, of leisure, of waiting and being patient. But that means, of thinking.” In his sickness, he stopped reading and started thinking. Looking back on his life, Nietzsche said that he was never happier with himself than in the sickest and most painful periods of his life.

questions.prompt: What did Nietzsche feel was happening during illness?
questions.promptZh: Nietzsche 觉得患病期间自己发生了什么变化？
options: He felt increasingly estranged from his own identity.
He claimed that every ill person makes exactly the same discovery.
He described a physical return to a named hometown.
He was returning to his natural self.
optionsZh: 他感到越来越疏离自己的身份。
他说每个患者都必有完全相同的发现。
他描述实际搬回一个明确命名的故乡。
他正回到自然的自我。
analyses: A returning to his natural self 与越来越疏离相反。
B he felt 是个人体验，不是每位患者的统一发现。
C natural self 不是地名或搬家记录。
D returning to his natural self 直接对应，且保留这是他的感受。

vocabulary.meaning: 本来的自我；自然的自己
vocabulary.context: 此处谈自我体验，而非野生环境或国籍变化。
vocabulary.example: The break from routine helped him feel closer to his natural self.

questions.evidenceQuote: During illness, he felt that he was returning to his natural self. “Looking from the perspective of the sick toward healthier concepts and values and, conversely, looking again from the fullness and self-assurance of a rich life down into the secret work of the instinct of decadence…Now I know how, have the know-how, to reverse perspectives.” Nietzsche credited his illness as a source of perspective change and wisdom, suggesting that adversity has the potential to generate psychological richness.

questions.prompt: What ability is emphasised in Nietzsche's quotation about looking in opposite directions?
questions.promptZh: Nietzsche 关于朝两个方向观察的引语强调什么能力？
options: Reversing perspectives between sickness and a fuller, more self-assured life.
Proving that only one perspective can ever have any value.
Avoiding every comparison between illness and healthier values.
Predicting the exact medical outcome of every illness from a quotation.
optionsZh: 在疾病与更充盈自信的人生之间转换视角。
证明只有一种视角在任何时候有价值。
回避疾病与较健康价值之间的一切比较。
从一句引语预测每种疾病的确切医学结局。
analyses: A conversely、looking again 与 reverse perspectives 都强调双向转换。
B 与 reverse 及前后两个观察方向相反。
C 引语正作这种对照，并非回避。
D 是哲学式自述，不是疾病预测模型，也没有确切结局数据。

vocabulary.meaning: 反过来说；从相反方向看
vocabulary.context: 引入另一观察方向，区别表示单向因果的 therefore。
vocabulary.example: He considered the healthy from the sick perspective and, conversely, the sick from the healthy one.

questions.evidenceQuote: During illness, he felt that he was returning to his natural self. “Looking from the perspective of the sick toward healthier concepts and values and, conversely, looking again from the fullness and self-assurance of a rich life down into the secret work of the instinct of decadence…Now I know how, have the know-how, to reverse perspectives.” Nietzsche credited his illness as a source of perspective change and wisdom, suggesting that adversity has the potential to generate psychological richness.

questions.prompt: Which award does the passage say Kahneman won?
questions.promptZh: 文中说 Kahneman 获得哪项奖？
options: The 1974 Nobel Prize in economics.
The 2002 Nobel Prize in literature.
The 2002 Nobel Prize in economics.
The 2022 Nobel Prize in economics.
optionsZh: 1974年诺贝尔经济学奖。
2002年诺贝尔文学奖。
2002年诺贝尔经济学奖。
2022年诺贝尔经济学奖。
analyses: A 1974是后文论文年份，不能替换获奖年。
B 年份相同但领域错；原文为 economics。
C 2002 与 economics 都由原句直接给出。
D 2022是后文论文引用统计年份，不能挪为获奖年。

vocabulary.meaning: 赢得；获得奖项
vocabulary.context: 在此指获诺贝尔经济学奖，不是赢得一次体育比赛。
vocabulary.example: The researcher won an award for work in economics.

questions.evidenceQuote: Daniel Kahneman won the 2002 Nobel Prize in economics. With Amos Tversky, he published a series of influential papers in the 1970s and 1980s, establishing himself as one of the most prominent psychologists in the world. His papers changed not just how psychologists think about human cognition, but also how economists think about rationality, the foundational assumption in much of modern economics.

questions.prompt: Which description of Kahneman's collaboration is given?
questions.promptZh: 文中如何描述 Kahneman 的合作研究？
options: He published influential papers with Amos Tversky in the 1970s and 1980s.
He published only with Nietzsche in 1869.
He became prominent before writing any paper with any collaborator.
He and Tversky worked only on classical language history.
optionsZh: 他与 Amos Tversky 在 1970、1980 年代发表了有影响的论文。
他仅与 Nietzsche 在 1869 年发表论文。
他在与任何人合作发表任何论文之前已因此成名。
他与 Tversky 只研究古典语言历史。
analyses: A 合作者、两年代和 influential papers 均对应原句。
B 把上一人物与任命年份混入此人的论文。
C establishing himself 把声望与所述论文联系，不是完全否认论文作用。
D 语言史属于前面 Nietzsche 的教席释义，不是这组论文的唯一课题。

vocabulary.meaning: 有影响力的；能改变他人认识或工作的
vocabulary.context: 修饰论文影响，不能直接理解为每个结论对每个人无例外成立。
vocabulary.example: The influential papers changed how researchers framed the problem.
collocations: one of the most prominent psychologists

questions.evidenceQuote: Daniel Kahneman won the 2002 Nobel Prize in economics. With Amos Tversky, he published a series of influential papers in the 1970s and 1980s, establishing himself as one of the most prominent psychologists in the world. His papers changed not just how psychologists think about human cognition, but also how economists think about rationality, the foundational assumption in much of modern economics.

questions.prompt: Which list matches the three heuristics described in the 1974 paper?
questions.promptZh: 哪一组符合 1974 年论文所述的三种启发式？
options: Representativeness, creativity, and classical philology.
Availability, Nobel selection, and medical recovery.
Representativeness, availability, and anchoring and adjustment.
Anchoring, adjustment, availability, and a fourth heuristic called representativeness.
optionsZh: 代表性、创造力、古典语文学。
可得性、诺奖评选、疾病康复。
代表性、可得性、锚定与调整。
锚定、调整、可得性，以及称为代表性的第四种启发式。
analyses: A 后两项并非本句三种启发式名称。
B 把本章其他主题混为启发式列表。
C 三项完整对应；anchoring and adjustment 为第三项的组合名称。
D 原文 three，不能把第三组合名拆成两种再计为四种。

vocabulary.meaning: 启发式；判断时采用的简化规则
vocabulary.context: 这里是三种命名的判断规则，不是保证每次正确的严格算法。
vocabulary.example: The study examined heuristics used when people make judgments.

questions.evidenceQuote: For instance, in one widely cited 1974 paper, Tversky and Kahneman described three heuristics: the representativeness heuristic, the availability heuristic, and the anchoring and adjustment heuristic, each of which has generated thousands of further research papers. (This 1974 Science paper was cited by 4,851 papers published in 2022 alone, an indication of its enduring influence.)

questions.prompt: How old was Kahneman when he escaped Nazi-occupied Paris, according to the passage?
questions.promptZh: 按原文，Kahneman 逃离纳粹占领的 Paris 时几岁？
options: Ninety, the age mentioned in the preceding sentence.
Seven.
Twenty-four, the age of Nietzsche's appointment.
The passage gives no age for this escape.
optionsZh: 九十岁，即前句所说年龄。
七岁。
二十四岁，即 Nietzsche 获任教席的年龄。
原文未给这次逃离时的年龄。
analyses: A 九十是去世年龄，不能挪为童年逃离年龄。
B when he was seven 明确标出。
C 混淆人物与事件。
D 原句直接给 seven；这里只依据书中历史叙述，不扩写未提供的逃离细节。

vocabulary.meaning: 逃离；脱离危险的地方或处境
vocabulary.context: 与 Nazi-occupied Paris 搭配，指战时经历，不是漏掉一次普通会议。
vocabulary.example: The family escaped from the occupied city.

questions.evidenceQuote: But Kahneman, who died at age ninety in 2024, was not just a Nobel laureate. He had an extraordinary personal story. He escaped Nazi-occupied Paris when he was seven. In his Nobel biography, Kahneman recalled a scary incident: “It must have been late 1941 or early 1942.

questions.prompt: How precisely does Kahneman date the frightening incident in his recollection?
questions.promptZh: Kahneman 在回忆中把惊险事件的时间说得多精确？
options: He supplies a verified exact day and hour in 1941.
He says it occurred only after the war had ended.
He places it unambiguously in the middle of 1944.
He estimates that it must have been late 1941 or early 1942.
optionsZh: 给出 1941 年经核实的确切日期和时刻。
说仅在战后发生。
毫不含糊地放在 1944 年中。
他估计应是 1941 年底或 1942 年初。
analyses: A late...or early... 未提供确切日时。
B 两候选时段均不是战后。
C 1944 属后面父亲去世的年份，不能移作此事。
D must have been 在回忆中表示对过去的推断，or 保留时间范围；不是要求事件在某时发生的命令。

vocabulary.meaning: 回忆；回顾过去发生的事
vocabulary.context: 标出叙述来源为其传记中的记忆，不表示现在重新进行了实验。
vocabulary.example: He recalled the incident but was uncertain of the precise date.

questions.evidenceQuote: But Kahneman, who died at age ninety in 2024, was not just a Nobel laureate. He had an extraordinary personal story. He escaped Nazi-occupied Paris when he was seven. In his Nobel biography, Kahneman recalled a scary incident: “It must have been late 1941 or early 1942.

questions.prompt: What did Kahneman do to his sweater before walking home?
questions.promptZh: Kahneman 走回家前对毛衣做了什么？
options: He turned his brown sweater inside out.
He bought a black uniform and replaced the sweater.
He left his sweater at home before visiting his friend.
He kept the sweater unchanged with its original outside still facing out.
optionsZh: 他把棕色毛衣里外翻转。
他买黑制服替换毛衣。
他去朋友家前就把毛衣留在家中。
他完全没翻动毛衣，原来的外面仍朝外。
analyses: A turned...inside out 与 brown sweater 直接对应动作及对象。
B 黑制服是后面士兵的，不是他购买换穿。
C 原句在回家路前翻面，不是之前留家。
D inside out 是已翻面的动作，与保持原样相反。

vocabulary.meaning: 里外翻转；把内面翻到外面
vocabulary.context: 此处为衣物翻面的实际动作，不是深入了解某事的固定用法。
vocabulary.example: She turned the sweater inside out before washing it.
collocations: turned my brown sweater inside out

questions.evidenceQuote: Jews were required to wear the Star of David and to obey a 6 p.m. curfew. I had gone to play with a Christian friend and had stayed too late. I turned my brown sweater inside out to walk the few blocks home.

questions.prompt: What did Kahneman see while walking down the empty street?
questions.promptZh: Kahneman 走在空街上时看见什么？
options: His Christian friend walking beside him in the street.
A German soldier moving away without approaching him.
A German soldier coming towards him.
His father leaving Drancy with his employer.
optionsZh: 身旁并肩走在街上的基督徒朋友。
一名正走远、未接近他的德国士兵。
一名朝他走来的德国士兵。
与雇主离开Drancy的父亲。
analyses: A 前文曾与朋友玩不等于此刻朋友也在路上。
B 身份相近但方向反了；approaching是接近。
C German soldier approaching 给身份与接近动作。
D 父亲拘禁与获释在后面另一段，不是空街所见。

vocabulary.meaning: 接近；朝某人或某处走来
vocabulary.context: 在 saw 后描述士兵当时的动作，不是已离开的方向。
vocabulary.example: He saw a stranger approaching along the quiet street.

questions.evidenceQuote: As I was walking down an empty street, I saw a German soldier approaching. He was wearing the black uniform that I had been told to fear more than others—the one worn by specially recruited SS soldiers. As I came closer to him, trying to walk fast, I noticed that he was looking at me intently. Then he beckoned me over, picked me up, and hugged me.

questions.prompt: Why was the black uniform especially frightening in Kahneman's recollection?
questions.promptZh: Kahneman 的回忆中，黑制服为何尤其令人害怕？
options: It was identified as the uniform of his school friends.
He had been told to fear it more than others; it was worn by specially recruited SS soldiers.
He says the uniform guaranteed that its wearer knew his name.
It had been given to him by his mother as a harmless disguise.
optionsZh: 它被认作学校朋友的制服。
他曾被告知应比其他制服更害怕它；这是特招 SS 士兵穿的制服。
他说该制服保证穿着者知道他的名字。
它是母亲给他的无害伪装。
analyses: A 该制服对应 SS 士兵，而非学校同伴。
B relative clause 交代被教导害怕，破折号后识别制服所属；保持回忆视角。
C 制服身份不证明士兵知道孩子名字。
D 穿着者是士兵，不是母亲交给孩子的衣服。

vocabulary.meaning: 特别招募的；专门选募的
vocabulary.context: 修饰 SS soldiers，不能读成随机分入实验条件。
vocabulary.example: The passage identifies a uniform worn by specially recruited soldiers.

questions.evidenceQuote: As I was walking down an empty street, I saw a German soldier approaching. He was wearing the black uniform that I had been told to fear more than others—the one worn by specially recruited SS soldiers. As I came closer to him, trying to walk fast, I noticed that he was looking at me intently. Then he beckoned me over, picked me up, and hugged me.

questions.prompt: What did Kahneman notice while trying to walk quickly past the approaching soldier?
questions.promptZh: 试着快步走、接近士兵时，Kahneman 注意到什么？
options: The soldier had already left without noticing him.
His own mother had arrived to stop the encounter.
The soldier had already identified the star hidden inside his sweater.
The soldier was looking at him intently.
optionsZh: 士兵已离开，完全未注意他。
他的母亲已赶到阻止这次相遇。
士兵已经认出了他藏在毛衣内侧的星标。
士兵正专注地看着他。
analyses: A looking at me intently 与完全未注意相反。
B 未记母亲此时到场。
C intently只说明专注地看；后面孩子担心星标被发现，不是确认士兵已识别。
D noticed that 后直接给观察；专注看不等于已经识别毛衣内侧标记，原句未确认其所知。

vocabulary.meaning: 专注地；目不转睛地
vocabulary.context: 说注视程度，不说明注视者确切知道什么或抱有何种动机。
vocabulary.example: The stranger looked at him intently without explaining why.

questions.evidenceQuote: As I was walking down an empty street, I saw a German soldier approaching. He was wearing the black uniform that I had been told to fear more than others—the one worn by specially recruited SS soldiers. As I came closer to him, trying to walk fast, I noticed that he was looking at me intently. Then he beckoned me over, picked me up, and hugged me.

questions.prompt: What does Kahneman explicitly recall about the soldier's speech?
questions.promptZh: 关于士兵讲话，Kahneman 明确回忆了什么？
options: He spoke in German with great emotion.
He gave a fully quoted explanation in French that Kahneman reports word for word.
He remained entirely silent throughout the encounter.
He told Kahneman in English that he knew the star was hidden.
optionsZh: 他用德语带着强烈感情讲话。
他用法语解释，Kahneman 逐字报告完整内容。
他在整个相遇中完全沉默。
他用英语告诉 Kahneman 已知隐藏星标。
analyses: A great emotion 与 in German 两项准确。
B 当前句未给逐字讲话内容，且语言是 German。
C speaking 与全程沉默相反。
D 未给英语或发现星标的声明，不能把孩子的担忧当士兵已说出的事实。

vocabulary.meaning: 情感；强烈的感情反应
vocabulary.context: great emotion 交代讲话情绪强度，不足以单独确认其具体思想。
vocabulary.example: He spoke with emotion, though the listener did not report his exact words.

questions.evidenceQuote: I was terrified that he would notice the star inside my sweater. He was speaking to me with great emotion, in German. When he put me down, he opened his wallet, showed me a picture of a boy, and gave me some money.” It was a close call.

questions.prompt: Which sequence follows the soldier putting Kahneman down?
questions.promptZh: 士兵把 Kahneman 放下后，发生哪组按序动作？
options: He gave money, hid the wallet, and took a picture of Kahneman.
He found the star, called another soldier, and arrested the boy.
He opened his wallet, showed a picture of a boy, and gave some money.
He returned the boy's wallet and demanded payment for the photograph.
optionsZh: 他先给钱，藏起钱包，再给 Kahneman 拍照。
他发现星标，叫来另一士兵并抓捕孩子。
他打开钱包，展示男孩照片，并给一些钱。
他归还孩子钱包，并为照片索款。
analyses: A 动作先后错，且 showed picture 不是现场拍照。
B 文中没有发现或逮捕，不能用恐惧替代实际叙事。
C opened、showed、gave 的顺序和对象都保留；未自行认定照片中的男孩是谁。
D his wallet 指士兵的钱包，给钱也不是索款。

vocabulary.meaning: 钱包；随身装钱或卡片的小包
vocabulary.context: 这里由士兵打开，装有他展示的照片，不是孩子交回的物品。
vocabulary.example: He opened his wallet and took out an old photograph.

questions.evidenceQuote: I was terrified that he would notice the star inside my sweater. He was speaking to me with great emotion, in German. When he put me down, he opened his wallet, showed me a picture of a boy, and gave me some money.” It was a close call.

questions.prompt: What belief did Kahneman say was reinforced when he went home?
questions.promptZh: Kahneman 说回家时什么看法得到加强？
options: Every member of every military organisation always behaves kindly.
His mother's view that people are endlessly complicated and interesting.
The view that one encounter makes all future people entirely predictable.
The belief that his mother had no influence on his interest in people.
optionsZh: 每个军队组织的每个人总友善行事。
母亲所说人无穷复杂且有趣的看法。
一次相遇使将来所有人都完全可预测的看法。
母亲对他关注人毫无影响的看法。
analyses: A 一次个人遭遇不支持对组织每人的普遍判断，且引语强调复杂。
B more certain than ever...mother was right 后给观点内容，准确保留归属。
C complicated 与完全可预测不同。
D 原句肯定母亲的看法，后句也归功于她的启发。

vocabulary.meaning: 复杂的；难以用单一简单判断概括的
vocabulary.context: 修饰人性，不是断言每个人都难以相处或可完全预测。
vocabulary.example: The encounter left him thinking that people were complicated.

questions.evidenceQuote: Kahneman went on to say, “I went home more certain than ever that my mother was right: people were endlessly complicated and interesting.” He credited his mother for inspiring him to become a psychologist.

questions.prompt: What distinction is important in the account of Kahneman's father's internment?
questions.promptZh: 关于 Kahneman 父亲被拘禁，哪种区分重要？
options: He was interned in Vichy and was never threatened with transfer.
He was sent straight to Palestine as a punishment while the war continued.
The sentence proves that he was actually sent to the extermination camp as planned.
He was interned in Drancy and was supposed to be sent to an extermination camp; the wording describes an intended transfer.
optionsZh: 他被拘禁于 Vichy，从未面临转送。
战争中他被直接送去 Palestine 作为惩罚。
本句证明他确实按计划被送进灭绝营。
他被拘禁于 Drancy，并原定送往灭绝营；措辞描述的是拟议转送。
analyses: A 拘禁地为 Drancy，且 supposed to be sent 明确威胁。
B Palestine 是后面战后家人迁移，不是本句处置。
C supposed to 不等于已完成；父亲实际获释的情况在上下文另有交代。
D 保留拘禁事实及原定转送的状态，不把意向程序偷换为已发生的转送。

vocabulary.meaning: 被拘禁；在战争等背景下被限制自由
vocabulary.context: 此处不是在机构实习的 intern，而是父亲的战时拘禁遭遇。
vocabulary.example: The account describes relatives who were interned during the war.

questions.evidenceQuote: Kahneman’s father was interned in Drancy and was supposed to be sent to an extermination camp.

questions.prompt: Which route and trigger for another escape are described?
questions.promptZh: 原文描述了怎样的逃离路线及再次逃离的触发事件？
options: The family went to Vichy, then fled again to central France after the Germans arrived.
The family went first to central France and then to Vichy after the war.
The family stayed in Vichy permanently because no German forces arrived.
The family moved directly from Drancy to Palestine before reaching Vichy.
optionsZh: 家人先逃到 Vichy，德军到来后又逃往法国中部。
家人战后先去法国中部，再到 Vichy。
家人在 Vichy 永久停留，因为德军从未到来。
家人未到 Vichy 就从 Drancy 直迁 Palestine。
analyses: A Then...Vichy、after Germans arrived、once more...center of France 三项对应。
B 路线倒置并加上战后时间。
C had to escape once more 与永久停留相反。
D 混合父亲拘禁地与后续家人迁移，漏掉本句两段逃离；不提前将尚未配题的后句算作直接覆盖。

vocabulary.meaning: 再一次；又一次
vocabulary.context: 此处说明 Vichy 之后的再次逃离，不是首次到达或原地不动。
vocabulary.example: After the danger returned, the family had to escape once more.

questions.evidenceQuote: Then his family escaped to Vichy, but after the Germans arrived, they had to escape once more to the center of France.
